_readme: The database contract: what production ACTUALLY IS, read out of the catalog.
The unit suite pins what each migration SAYS. Fifty migrations redefine the
same functions over and over, so a pin on a superseded generation stays green
forever while the live object has moved on. This file is the other half: every
entry below was read out of pg_proc / pg_policy / has_*_privilege / pg_constraint
/ pg_indexes / pg_trigger / pg_publication_tables / cron.job against the live
database, and `npm run verify:db` re-reads exactly those catalogs and diffs.
Rules for editing this file:
- Change an entry only when a migration deliberately changed the object.
A diff here without a migration behind it is drift, not an update.
- knownGaps are NOT approvals. They record surplus privilege that exists
today so the verifier can ratchet: the gap set may shrink, never grow.
- bodyMd5 pins the WHOLE live pg_get_functiondef text of an entry, not
just needle presence. A migration that touches such a function must
update the md5 here in the same commit; unexplained drift fails.
- tests/db-contract.test.js keeps this file in lockstep with the migrations
offline, so a new grant/policy cannot land without an entry here.
Source of truth for `exec`: has_function_privilege(role, oid, 'EXECUTE') plus an
aclexplode() probe for grantee 0 (PUBLIC). Reachability of private.* also depends
on schema USAGE -- see schemaUsage below.

functions.note: 20260906030000. THE one article-level withholding predicate, taking the whole row rather than a column list a later column could fall out of: true for an authored article and for a derived article whose OWN originating Storage source holds a current ledger verdict, false for an unresolved (withheld) article, for a derived article whose source has lapsed, and — fail-closed — for a %rowtype variable a `select ... into` left unset. Every article-level gate is routed through it, so private.knowledge_source_verdict_current is no longer reachable from an article row except through this check and no gate can consult a source the record has withdrawn.

20260906030000. The ONE door out of article-level withholding, written once so "a withheld article resurfaces only through a reviewed reconciliation from an inspected source" is a property of a single function. For an unresolved article it returns the version-zero CHANGED-CLAUSE candidate (status 'draft') whose own content_origin is 'derived' and whose own source holds a current verdict; for every other article it returns nothing. The 'draft' shape is load-bearing and its proof is 20260906029000's: the changed-clause branch is the only writer of a version-zero draft row and every text value it inserts comes out of p_source_id's own inspected bytes, whereas a RETIREMENT candidate copies the ARTICLE's text — which on a withheld article is the withheld text itself — so bodyForbids pins the retirement shape out of this door.

The ONLY way a restore_chapter_kb_revision idempotency receipt becomes a response again. It refuses outright any receipt carrying an article content key (title, article_ref, body, keywords), which retires every content-bearing receipt written before 20260906028000, then rebuilds the response through a CURRENT gated read: the article must still exist in the receipt's chapter and must not be sample (P0002), and its current knowledge_source_id must hold a current ledger verdict (42501 'file inspection required') — the same refusals the primary path raises. Granted to no role; it is reachable only from its security-definer caller. Since 20260906030000 the gated re-read is the article-level withholding predicate, and it keeps both refusal shapes: a withheld article answers P0002 'not found', the same answer the primary path gives it, and a lapsed verdict keeps 42501.

Service-only write-side recheck: derives the owning organization-knowledge object from a source id, locks its storage.objects row, then evaluates the ledger predicate coalesced to false so a concurrent verdict change serializes against the completion write and an unknown answer is a refusal.

Staff-only bounded revision history follows an explicit same-organization review chapter, with the current chapter retained as the legacy default. Since 20260906028000 every revision carries its own content origin, so each derived row is gated on ITS OWN source: history lifted from a source that has since lapsed is not listed even while the article sits on a clean replacement source. Unresolved-origin rows — historical revisions whose true source cannot be proved — are excluded outright and are never treated as authored, and contentOrigin is projected so a reviewer can see which rows are Storage-derived. 20260906029000 adds reconciledBySourceId to that projection: a version-zero retirement candidate is gated on the ARTICLE's own source, because its text is a copy of the article, and the agreement that proposed the removal is reported separately instead of being smuggled into the content column. 20260906030000 makes the article-level precondition the withholding predicate plus the one re-establishment door: a withheld article answers with the same P0002 an absent one does, unless it carries a reviewed re-establishment candidate, in which case that candidate — and nothing else, because the rest of its history is 'unresolved' — is listed.

functions.note: Service-only, chapter-serialized CBA reconciliation re-establishes the originating object's ledger verdict under its Storage row lock, then derives stable clause keys, preserves a collision-free contiguous agreement order range without versioning identical draft retries, keeps published and independently authored articles, clears stale candidates, and stages changed or missing verified clauses for explicit review. Since 20260906028000 every revision it writes states its content origin explicitly. Since 20260906029000 CONTENT provenance and DECISION provenance are separate columns: a retirement candidate for an omitted clause is a COPY OF THE ARTICLE'S OWN TEXT, so it keeps the article's own knowledge_source_id and records the reconciling agreement in reconciled_by_source_id, while a changed-clause candidate carries the replacement's own normalized text and names p_source_id in both. Stamping the retirement copy with p_source_id (pinned out by bodyForbids) let confirmation republish one source's language under another's provenance and left that history listable once the originating source lapsed. Each canonical snapshot still takes the article's own origin and knowledge_source_id, so Storage-derived history can never be read back as authored. Since 20260906030000 every ARTICLE it writes states its content origin in the same statement that names its source, every canonical revision it appends takes the article's stated origin rather than re-deriving it, and it is the only path that re-establishes a WITHHELD article: such an article is treated as changed even when the incoming clause is byte-identical (byte-identity proves nothing about where the withheld bytes came from), and a withheld draft is never skipped as an identical retry, so the staged candidate carries this agreement's own inspected bytes and a reviewer's restore re-sources the row. A withheld article stages NO retirement candidate and is not swept into 'retired': both would have to re-assert the provenance claim this record withdrew.

functions.note: Idempotent explicit-chapter staff review can draft or verify imported changes, confirm retirement, or dismiss a proposed removal without changing canonical content. THIS NOTE PINS ORDER, NOT MERELY THE PRESENCE OF PREDICATES. The single value the idempotency branch is allowed to return is private.knowledge_revision_restore_receipt(chapter, cached), which re-reads the article and re-evaluates the ledger verdict BEFORE anything crosses the boundary, so no cached replay can precede a provenance check; `return cached;` is pinned OUT by bodyForbids, and since 20260906028000 the receipt stores content-free lifecycle metadata only (articleId, newVersion, status, restoredRevisionId, action). TWO SEPARATE MECHANISMS BIND A RECEIPT TO ITS ACTOR AND THEY MUST NOT BE CONFLATED. private.mi1_w2_operation_receipts is an ACTOR-KEYED VIEW over private.mi1_w2_operation_receipt_rows, whose primary key carries actor_user_id, so a SECOND actor replaying the same key sees no receipt at all: that replay is a distinct operation, it runs the full gated path, it writes its own receipt, and it is NOT refused. The request payload carrying auth.uid() is what raises 22023, and only for the case that namespace does not cover — a receipt visible under the caller's OWN actor id that was stored for a different request — which is also why every pre-20260906028000 receipt refuses on a same-actor replay. An unresolved-origin revision is refused with the same P0002 the hidden-history listing answers with; the article's own source AND the candidate revision's OWN source must each hold a current verdict; and the restored article's provenance is set to the revision's own content source (knowledge_source_id = restored_source), with the previous coalesce onto an unrelated current source pinned out by bodyForbids. Since 20260906029000 a version-zero retirement candidate carries the ARTICLE's own source, so confirming a retirement keeps the article on that source and writes the canonical retirement revision derived from it; once that source lapses both confirmation and dismissal are refused 42501 'file inspection required' like any other content-bearing answer for lapsed text, and public.retire_chapter_kb_article remains the staff cleanup path. 20260906030000 adds the article-level withholding and its ONE door. A withheld article answers with the same P0002 an absent one does, so this RPC is not an oracle for withheld text; the single exception is the exact version-zero changed-clause candidate private.knowledge_article_reestablishment_candidate names, whose text is the incoming agreement's own inspected bytes rather than a copy of the article. On that path the article's own (withdrawn) source gates nothing and only the candidate's own source is checked, and the article's content_origin is written from the revision's — 'authored' or 'derived', never 'unresolved' — so this is also the one writer that lifts article-level withholding.

functions.note: MFA-aware staff-only create/edit/publish path accepts only the current chapter or an explicitly selected same-organization chapter; every successful save appends an immutable revision. The UPDATE branch is the second publication route to a Storage-derived row, so it refuses with the same 42501 'file inspection required' as restore_chapter_kb_revision once the originating source's verdict has lapsed; a new article has no provenance and is unaffected. Since 20260906028000 the appended revision records the article's content origin and knowledge_source_id, so a staff edit of Storage-derived language is written as 'derived' and stays bound to that file's verdict rather than being laundered into authored text. Since 20260906030000 the create branch states content_origin = 'authored' explicitly (the column has no default), the appended revision takes the article's own stated origin instead of re-deriving it from the source column, and the update branch is gated on the whole withholding predicate. Its two halves keep the two refusal shapes this record already established and neither is an oracle: a WITHHELD article answers exactly as an absent one does (42501 'knowledge article is not available in this chapter'), while a derived article whose source has lapsed keeps 42501 'file inspection required'.

functions.note: Chapter-publishing staff create/edit/publish their own chapter's public profile. The chapter lookup binds chapters.organization_id to the caller's organization, so a foreign chapter id is never claimable even before its profile exists. Conflict updates keep kind='chapter' and the caller organization so a raced foreign insert cannot be rewritten, and they never touch the localized region columns, so copy-only edits preserve translated public region content. A regionless chapter inserts NULL regions rather than failing: this migration replaces public_site_records_shape so a chapter row may carry either both localized regions or neither, matching the public renderer's missing-region handling. The p_expected_updated_at guard refuses a stale two-editor submit with 'chapter profile changed since load' instead of silently overwriting the first save; a form loaded while the profile was absent passes p_expected_missing, so a concurrent second create is refused the same way rather than overwriting the first, and a NULL version without p_expected_missing is rejected.

mfaCoverage.note: REQ-UG-DEFINER-MFA-AUDIT. Every SECURITY DEFINER function in schema PUBLIC reachable by authenticated bypasses RLS (including the mfa_assurance restrictive policy), so each must force MFA step-up itself -- directly via private.mfa_satisfied() or transitively via member_has_role (which carries the term) -- or be listed exempt with a reason. A public function that is neither covered nor listed FAILS the sweep, so a member RPC added later cannot ship unguarded. `pending` is the ratchet for the staged rollout: it WARNs and must shrink to empty as batches 2-4 land. It DID -- batch 4 (20260725200000) drained it, and it stays empty: a new entry needs a scheduled batch and an edit to the exact-empty pin in tests/mfa-guard-capability-rpcs.test.js. Scope is PUBLIC only: private definer functions reachable by authenticated (award_member_points and other trigger/helper functions) are internal, run inside already-guarded callers or trigger contexts, and their authenticated-EXECUTE ACL is a separate concern tracked by knownGaps.publicExecuteOnPrivateFunctions -- an MFA guard on them would be wrong.

exempt.delete_my_native_push_installation: Sign-out/disable safety path: requires the live caller and server-derived current-session handle to match the account UUID and opaque handle captured by the client action, plus a device-held random installation UUID; it deletes only the exact auth.uid()- and session-owned row and returns one uniform false result for stale same-user, foreign, or unknown identifiers. Requiring MFA would prevent cleanup while the session is awaiting step-up.
exempt.prepare_my_signout: Sign-out safety path: both scopes require the live caller to match the expected account UUID captured by the client action; the local scope also requires a live current Auth session and deletes only auth.uid()-owned rows bound to that session, while the global scope still performs an explicit MFA check. Requiring MFA for local cleanup would retain push endpoints while the session is awaiting step-up.

schemaUsage.note: Load-bearing false. cron.job_run_details grants SELECT,DELETE to PUBLIC (its relacl carries the empty-grantee item '=rd/supabase_admin'), and cron.schedule / cron.unschedule are PUBLIC EXECUTE and SECURITY INVOKER. None of it is reachable because no client role can enter the schema. This row is the assertion that keeps it that way -- a single 'grant usage on schema cron' would arm all of it at once, including DELETE over the notification dispatcher's run history.

USAGE here is stock Supabase and is NOT the control that matters: net.http_request_queue grants INSERT to anon with RLS OFF, and net.http_post is SECURITY INVOKER with EXECUTE to both client roles. What makes that unreachable is that PostgREST exposes only 'public, graphql_public' -- see knownGaps.vendorSchemaClientGrants.why and the roleSettings pin on authenticator.
Required: the mfa_assurance restrictive policy calls private.mfa_satisfied() as the invoking role. This is why a surplus PUBLIC EXECUTE inside private.* is not purely theoretical -- see knownGaps.

roleSettings.note: The pgrst.* pin. PostgREST reads pgrst.db_schemas / db_pre_request / db_anon_role from this role's pg_db_role_setting when present, and supautils allowlists 'pgrst.*' for supabase_privileged_role -- which postgres belongs to (verified live 2026-07-26). So ONE 'alter role authenticator set pgrst.db_schemas' in a migration would expose schema net (INSERT for anon, RLS OFF) and nothing else in this repo would see it. Exact-set assertion, both directions. BOUNDARY, deliberately written down: this does NOT cover the Supabase dashboard's Exposed schemas field, which is service configuration leaving no catalog trace -- pg_db_role_setting is empty of pgrst.* precisely because the live value lives outside the database, so a dashboard change keeps this check green.

restrictiveOnEveryRlsTable.note: Applied by a DO loop at migration time, so a table created by a LATER migration silently lacks it. Nothing in the offline suite can see that; only this catalog sweep can.

protectedRelationPolicyReferences.note: A storage.objects policy that directly names a client-revoked metadata relation can fail privilege checks while PostgreSQL evaluates unrelated bucket policies. Protected-table reads belong behind narrowly executable bucket-first SECURITY DEFINER predicates.

constraints.note: Canonical history and the single version-zero review candidate retain deterministic uniqueness; existing SAMPLE reseeding continues to target this stable constraint.

constraints.name: member_kb_article_revisions_authored_has_no_source
constraints.note: Authored means no Storage provenance at all, so this constraint keeps a null source on every authored row. It is NOT the withholding rule and must not be read as one: a row whose origin could not be proved is recorded 'unresolved', and since 20260906029000 an unresolved row retains NO content provenance at all — member_kb_article_revisions_unresolved_names_no_source forces its knowledge_source_id to null at every version. The only provenance a withheld row keeps is DECISION provenance, and only on a version-zero candidate, through reconciled_by_source_id.

constraints.name: member_kb_article_revisions_candidate_origin_known
constraints.note: 20260906029000 widened 20260906028000's candidate shape. A candidate staged by the current writer is derived and names the exact source its TEXT came out of, but EVERY legacy retirement candidate the one-shot backfill met had to be recorded 'unresolved' with NO source: its text was copied off the article under a source nothing recorded, and no timestamp on these rows is serialization order, so it is withheld from every reader instead of being called derived and gated on a guess. Its decision source survives in reconciled_by_source_id and nothing else does.

constraints.name: member_kb_article_revisions_content_origin_known
constraints.note: The explicit content-origin discriminator 20260906028000 added. The column is NOT NULL with NO DEFAULT, so no writer can classify Storage-derived text as authored by omission, and an origin this migration could not prove stays 'unresolved' rather than being guessed.

constraints.name: member_kb_article_revisions_derived_names_its_source
constraints.note: Replaces the retired equality constraint that forced every POSITIVE-version revision to a null source, which made canonical Storage-derived history indistinguishable from authored history and let a lapsed source's text stay listable and republishable once the article had moved to a clean source. A derived revision of any version must name its own source, which is what lets each row be gated on its own provenance.

constraints.name: member_kb_article_revisions_import_candidate_unique
constraints.note: A changed imported candidate is idempotent for its published article while canonical history keeps independent version uniqueness.

constraints.name: member_kb_article_revisions_reconciled_by_is_candidate
defContains: (reconciled_by_source_id IS NOT NULL) = (import_candidate_key IS NOT NULL)
constraints.note: 20260906029000. DECISION provenance is an iff over version-zero candidates: only a candidate may name the reconciliation that staged it, and every candidate must. A future writer therefore cannot let a candidate inherit somebody else's reconciliation by omission, and cannot attach a reconciler to a canonical revision that already states its own content source.

constraints.name: member_kb_article_revisions_unresolved_names_no_source
constraints.note: An unresolved row names no source at ANY version. Naming one is how a guess re-enters the schema; a null source keeps the row inert, and list_chapter_kb_revisions excludes it and restore_chapter_kb_revision refuses it P0002 regardless.

constraints.name: member_kb_article_revisions_version_shape
constraints.note: Canonical revisions use positive versions while the one pending imported update occupies a non-canonical version-zero review slot.

constraints.name: member_kb_articles_authored_has_no_source
constraints.note: Authored means no Storage provenance at all. It is NOT the withholding rule and must not be read as one: a withheld article is recorded 'unresolved' and KEEPS the knowledge_source_id it carries, because that value is real history — and because nulling it would make the row MORE visible, private.knowledge_source_verdict_current answering true for a null source by design (invariant 6). On a withheld row that value gates nothing.

_readme: Recorded, not approved. Each entry is surplus privilege that exists in production
today and is currently masked by another control (RLS, PostgREST schema exposure,
the absence of a SQL channel for the role). The verifier prints every one as a WARN
and FAILS if a gap appears that is not listed here -- the set may shrink, never grow.
Closing them is a migration, not an edit to this file.

surplusClientTableGrants.why: Supabase's stock `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on tables to anon, authenticated, service_role` fires on every CREATE TABLE. The migrations only ever ADD `grant select`; they never `revoke all` first, so each new table keeps INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE for authenticated. RLS masks the DML. It did NOT mask TRUNCATE, which is not a row operation and is never filtered by a policy -- that half was closed by 20260725220000, which revoked TRUNCATE on every granting table AND removed it from the postgres default ACL, so tables created by repo migrations (which run as postgres) are not born with it. supabase_admin's stock default ACL is out of postgres's reach; any table it creates would surface here as a NEW surplus key and fail the sweep. The other non-row bits of that same default ACL -- REFERENCES, TRIGGER and PG17's MAINTAIN, none of which RLS filters either -- were revoked by 20260726010000 (REQ-UG-REFTRIGGER-SWEEP-20260725), which also removed all three from the postgres default ACL, so repo-created tables are now born `arwd`; the sweeps below were widened to all eight privileges in the same commit, so a regrant of any of them goes red. UB-VOTE-01 closes four more gaps by revoking campaign-table DML and moving their intentional SELECT-only grants to tableGrants. REQ-UG-LEARNING-PERIOD-CASE-RECORDS-20261103 (20261104075000) closes member_case_updates: the member's note goes through add_my_case_update, and the table moves to tableGrants as SELECT only. Every remaining entry is RLS-masked DML only.

publicExecuteOnPrivateFunctions.why: These three never got the `revoke all on function ... from public` their siblings did, so they keep the default PUBLIC EXECUTE. authenticated HAS USAGE on schema private (mfa_assurance needs it), so the grant is not purely nominal. Two of the three are trigger functions, which Postgres refuses to call directly, and PostgREST does not expose the private schema -- that is what makes this a gap rather than an incident. notify_cosigners_on_approve left the set on 2026-07-28: its 20260728221544 re-emission carries the explicit revoke. issue_member_ballot_receipt left on 2026-08-08: 20260808230000 dropped the function outright (UB-VOTE-04). award_member_points and member_receipt_code left on 2026-11-10: 20261110021827 revoked PUBLIC and client EXECUTE from both SECURITY DEFINER entries, because a SQL login with USAGE on private and the default PUBLIC TEMP could attach the trigger to its own temporary table and run an implicit cast of its own as the definer (review K3-SOL-1). The remaining entry is SECURITY INVOKER and is called from a CHECK constraint.

vendorSchemaClientGrants.why: Client-role table privileges in schemas Supabase owns. Recorded EXACTLY, and deliberately NOT ratcheted the way surplusClientTableGrants is: postgres cannot revoke ANY of these, because their grantor is supabase_admin / supabase_storage_admin / supabase_realtime_admin and postgres is not a member of those roles. A revoke issued as postgres against them is a SILENT NO-OP -- proven live 2026-07-26 against storage.objects: no error, no warning, privileges byte-identical before and after. So a NEW-key-fails ratchet would redden this lane on every Supabase platform release with no fix available. Instead each recorded pair is asserted exactly on privileges + RLS + owner, and an UNRECORDED pair only WARNs. The owner assertion is load-bearing in its own right: an ownership change to postgres is the day a revoke becomes possible. Sharpest entry: net.http_request_queue grants INSERT to anon with RLS OFF, and net.http_post / http_get / http_delete are SECURITY INVOKER with EXECUTE to both client roles -- together a server-side-request-forgery primitive. It is unreachable ONLY because PostgREST exposes just 'public, graphql_public' (probed live: Accept-Profile: net returns PGRST106 Invalid schema, the public-schema control returns HTTP 200), and the single public function referencing net (public.get_notification_dispatch_health) grants EXECUTE to neither client role. That defence is service configuration rather than a grant -- and it is migration-reachable, which is what contract.roleSettings pins. Second sharpest: cron.job_run_details grants SELECT,DELETE to PUBLIC and cron.unschedule is PUBLIC EXECUTE SECURITY INVOKER, held back solely by schemaUsage cron=false for every client role. Supabase Storage migration 0073-revoke-grants-to-unused-operations (upstream https://github.com/supabase/storage/pull/1395, merged September 16, 2026) applied to production October 14, 2026 at 12:22:44 AM ET. It revoked TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER and, on PostgreSQL 17, MAINTAIN from anon/authenticated on storage.buckets, storage.objects and storage.buckets_analytics, leaving DELETE,INSERT,SELECT,UPDATE. Last deployed drift pass: run 38507552176 at 12:20:55 AM ET; first failure: run 38525044775 at 3:34:01 AM ET. SAMPLE remains on Storage migration 72 with the old full grants. This is a reviewed platform expectation correction; no application migration or hosted grant change is authorized.
vendorSchemaClientGrants.outOfContract: RLS state, policies and function grants inside these schemas are NOT asserted beyond the rls field recorded per entry. The repo cannot run 'alter table ... enable row level security' or 'create policy' on tables it does not own, so asserting a desired value would be permanently red with no available fix. net._http_response, net.http_request_queue and realtime.subscription are recorded with rls false for that reason -- recorded as-is, not endorsed.
